22.text: which is set on the central timber

27.text: The mast is supported by four stays

28.text: fastened to its top or passing

29.text: through a hole in it. The fore-

30.text: stays are joined together and simply slung over the end of the bow. The

31.text: back-stays are fastened to the middle strips by means of ivory blocks (Figs.

32.text: 44, a¹; 46, a¹; 46, b), which are occasionally replaced by loops of thong

35.text: The sail is large and square, and is fastened by loops to a yard.

36.text: It is hoisted by means of a stout seal-skin thong which is passed through a

37.text: hole in the top of the mast, sometimes with the aid of a pulley. Four slender

38.text: lines extend from the ends of the sail and yard to the stern, where they are

39.text: tied to the inside strip-lashings. By means of these lines the position of the sail

40.text: can be changed, enabling the boat to go with a side wind. The boat I

41.text: obtained has two sails, one above the other, with separate halyards and lines.
